summary: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and the Union Government have sanctioned new border infrastructure projects, including phase three of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) and multiple tactical bridges in Arunachal Pradesh, amid continuing military face-offs along the Line of Actual Control.

background.text: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) is a Central Armed Police Force raised in 1962, tasked with guarding the 3,488 km Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China.
The Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR) scheme was launched in 2005 (Phase-I) and expanded in September 2020 (Phase-II) following the Galwan clashes to bridge infrastructure deficits along the LAC.
The Union Budget provides dedicated capital outlays for Border Infrastructure and Management (BIM) and the Vibrant Villages Programme to reinforce frontier defenses and connectivity.

prelims_pointer.text: The Cabinet Committee on Security cleared ICBR-III, sanctioning 26 strategic border roads along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh.
The ITBP has authorised 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in the border districts of Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey in Arunachal Pradesh.
ITBP operates under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs for border security, counter-insurgency, and high-altitude disaster relief operations.

mains_question: Examine the significance of rapid border infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in countering security challenges posed by adversary build-ups, with special reference to India's northeastern frontier.

mains_points.text: Enhanced border infrastructure ensures tactical mobility and rapid logistics support for security forces confronting frequent face-offs along rugged stretches of the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh.
Counters the asymmetrical advantage gained by China's extensive modernisation of military logistics, road networks, and border infrastructure.
Calls for integrating niche technologies—such as drones and counter-drone systems—with traditional border infrastructure to address evolving technological modernization by adversaries.
Strategic investments under schemes like Border Infrastructure and Management support civilian connectivity, discouraging border out-migration and cementing territorial administration.
